_what: FINDING: the BattleGrid candle endpoint (get_coin_candles) RESTATED bars it had already served. Out-of-sample re-pull 2 (2026-09-02) was diffed, per the protocol, against every prior source (base corpus pulled 2026-08-29; re-pull 1 pulled 2026-08-30 - those two agreed with each other on 78-94 overlapping bars per series at the time). Every one of the 16 series now differs on previously served bars. This record holds every differing field verbatim (old = as served on 08-29/08-30 and stored in the repo; new = as served 2026-09-02 ~01:36Z and stored in repulls/2026-09-02/raw/).
when: 2026-09-02, handoff-plan session, Task 1 Step 3 (integrity check) - read-only; no platform write involved

volume_direction._note: every volume revision is an increase - consistent with trades being added to bars, not with re-pricing

summary.structure: The three 4h series (which reach back to 2026-08-16) show a clean start: 36-37 bars before 2026-08-22T08:00Z (SOL: 12:00Z) match EXACTLY on all five fields, and 42-46 of the 45-46 bars from there on differ. The 1h overlap (from 2026-08-28T21:00Z) lies entirely inside the affected range, so 3-24 of 27-28 bars per coin differ.
summary.magnitude: Volume: mostly <1% relative, max 34.7% (one MET bar), 14.5% (LDO), 8.5% (PEPE), 5.8% (CAKE), 4.7% (BTC 4h). Prices: 35 fields total (open 21, close 8, high 4, low 2), all tiny - max 0.23% (MELANIA open), BTC 1h close 78146->78145 (one tick).
summary.timing_inference: Base (08-29) and re-pull 1 (08-30) matched exactly on their overlap, including bars inside the now-affected range. So the served history changed AFTER 2026-08-30T00:xxZ and BEFORE 2026-09-02T01:36Z. Whether it was one discrete event (a backfill/re-aggregation from ~08-22) or a slow trickle that happened to be zero across 08-29->08-30 is NOT distinguishable from two pulls; a discrete event is the simpler reading. The CAUSE is unknown and not inferred.

transcription_ruled_out.why_it_matters: the 16 raw files were written by a subagent re-typing the tool responses; a transcription slip would look like a restatement
transcription_ruled_out.check_1_direct_recalls: get_coin_candles re-called from the main session for BTC 1h, BTC 4h and AIXBT 1h (~01:40Z); 45 values read directly off those responses (22 BTC 1h volumes + the 08-29T21:00 close, 15 BTC 4h volumes, 8 AIXBT bars incl. the restated opens) were compared programmatically to the saved files: 0 disagreements
transcription_ruled_out.check_2_1h_to_4h_aggregation: for BTC/ETH/SOL, every 4h bar fully covered by the pull's own 1h bars (24 per coin, 72 total) equals the exact aggregate of those 1h bars (open of first, close of last, max high, min low, summed volume to 1e-4): 0 inconsistent. Independently transcribed files that sum exactly are not mis-typed.
transcription_ruled_out.check_3_selectivity: OHLC fields matched the prior corpus on ~98.5% of overlap fields (2,365 of 2,400) while volume differed on most; a transcription failure would not select the volume field
transcription_ruled_out.verdict: the saved files faithfully hold what the platform served on 2026-09-02; the platform's served history changed

canonical_battery_response._note: by design - the script asserts that two sources never disagree on (close, volume) for the same timestamp. It was NOT modified. Numbers for the addendum come from repulls/analyze_repull_sensitivity.py, a copy that differs only in (a) an explicit collision POLICY (first-seen | latest) and (b) an optional run-1 event cutoff; THE pre-registered cell is identical under both policies (235 collisions resolved either way).

protocol_consequences_NOT_acted_on: the integrity check's 'any non-zero MISMATCH is a finding' rule is now known to fire on ordinary volume revisions; whether to compare OHLC strictly and volume with a tolerance, or to keep flagging and recording, is a protocol change for the user to decide
the canonical analyze_repull.py refuses the merged corpus; choosing a collision policy for it is a code change to a 'reuse unchanged' file - the user's call
prior-run numbers computed on first-seen values (run 1: n=9, 66.7%, +36.7) remain reproducible only under the first-seen policy; the raw files preserve both versions of every bar
_interpretation: Measured: the platform's candle history is not immutable; served values for closed bars from ~2026-08-22 onward were revised between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-02, upward in volume on 235 fields and by one to a few ticks in price on 35 fields. Inferred (not measured): the pattern fits late trade data being folded into existing bars in one pass. Unknown: the cause, whether it recurs, and whether older bars will be revised again. Consequence for the research: THE cell is unaffected by which version is used; the honesty consequence is that 'verified against the prior corpus' can no longer mean 'byte-identical'.
_erratum: The first commit of this record (cbe9ce8) and its message quoted 425 fields / volume 377 / open 28 / close 13 / high 5 / low 2. Those came from a diagnostic that compared each bar against BOTH prior sources and counted a bar twice when it sat in both. The programmatic counts in summary.fields_changed_total (270 fields: volume 235, open 21, close 8, high 4, low 2) are the correct ones; bar count (253), structure, magnitudes and THE cell were never affected.
_followup_same_day: Under the user's 2026-09-02 instruction to follow the best recommendation, the items under protocol_consequences_NOT_acted_on were then acted on: analyze_repull.py gained an explicit collision policy (POLICY=latest default, first, strict = the original refusal; any close restated >1% aborts under every policy), the sensitivity copy was removed once the canonical script reproduced the identical cell, verify_repull.py now writes records like this one automatically and fails only on gaps/dupes/zero overlap/price >1%, and the protocol carries a dated post-hoc amendment explaining why this is not goalpost movement (the cell was identical under both policies before the policy was chosen).
